name: 小白腰雨燕
illustrationTaxon: Apus nipalensis adult representative, runtime taxonomy retained

similarSpecies.distinction: Substantive identification/range/conservation read. 17–20cm sexes alike. Long scythe wings and long relatively deeply forked tail, all blackish brown apart contrasting WHITE RUMP band and indistinct pale throat, pale fringed underparts; substantially larger than House Swift. Nominate breeds Siberia/Kamchatka/NChina/Japan, winters Indonesia/Melanesia/Australia. kurodae (kanoi synonym treatment differs) EChina to Guangdong/SJapan/Taiwan/NPhilippines, winters Malaysia/Indonesia/Philippines. Western Guangdong/E Guangxi boundary obscured by Cook swift; map not occurrence polygon. LC stable globally despite local HK migrant decline, local offshore island breeding.

Substantive identification/range/conservation read. 13–14cm sexes alike. Representative innominatus blackish brown upperparts with paler GREY BROWN rump not white; dark crown vs paler grey-brown nape and dark eye area; underparts paler grey brown. Blunt wing tips, slightly notched tail closed; more fluttering than House Swift. Rump colour varies, dark-rumped birds within variation, light changes apparent colours. Breeds Himalaya to central China/Myanmar/N Thailand/SW China; winters Bangladesh/Malay peninsula. Regular nonbreeding S China/N Vietnam, vagrants Taiwan/Korea/Japan excluded partial map. LC stable; scarce increasing HK visitors all months.

rangeMap.note: Runtime retains House Swift Apus nipalensis, adult sexes alike, compact/stocky swift, white rump and pale chin/throat, shorter less scythe wings and short shallow forked tail unlike Pacific. Updated HKBWS lumps Oriental birds into Little Swift A.affinis nipalensis; explicitly local mainland-China nipalensis distribution Nepal east to SE China/south via Assam/SEAsia, resident Japan. Map conservatively selected Asian countries of nipalensis group only, NOT Africa/SWAsia of broader affinis. HKBWS global LC increasing pertains current lumped taxon, not asserted as split-nipalensis trend. Split LC independently crosschecked BirdGuides IOC10.2 record. HK local breeding/migrant decline not global IUCN category. World partial native-country overview only not precise occupancy/season or complete range.
